MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
September 16, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday,
September 16, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Councilmember Sanchez was absent. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public
Works Director Damasse, Community Services Director McPherron, Parks and Recreation
Director Harding, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the
motion.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmembers Savidan, Traina, Gazeley and Mayor Estrada.
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

3.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada presented the 2013 State of the City Address. Mayor Estrada stated that
although revenues remain stagnant, the City adopted a balanced budget for Fiscal Year 2013-
14 in June 2013, which was accomplished without the use of any reserve funds. Mayor
Estrada added that some new special funds were created as part of the budget including
$50,000 to start the Stephenson Center Capital Improvement Fund and $83,000 for
funding an emergency generator at city facilities.

  Page 1
 Mayor Estrada continued by saying that the City Council held a formal strategic planning workshop
and later that year approved Mission, Vision and Core Values Statement.

Mayor Estrada stated that in April of this year, after comprehensive offline testing and extensive
public outreach, the City began distribution of blended water from the Cypress Water Production
Facility and Well No. 5. The facility is running smoothly since April 2013 with very few
complaints from the public. Mayor Estrada stated that street improvements were identified by
the City Council as one of is highest priorities and over last year two major projects were
implemented –Crenshaw Lomita Boulevard Street Improvement Project and Eshelman Avenue
Street and Waterline Replacement Project. Mayor Estrada thanked staff and fellow
Councilmembers for working hard through the year.

Mayor Estrada declared September 17 through 23, 2013, as Constitution Week.

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers presented plaque from the Government Finance Officers
Association (GOFA) to the City’s Administrative Services Department and her staff for a
Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting for the City’s comprehensive
annual financial report (CAFR).

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Rani Martinez, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Commerce,
thanked Mayor Estrada for her service as Mayor and Councilmember. Ms. Martonez invited
those in attendance to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at
the Railroad Museum on Thursday, September 26, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, stated that she had been having problems with chlorine and
sulfur smell at her residence.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that during construction at Lomita Blvd. and Crenshaw
there were no signs posted that Crenshaw was closed and traffic was diverted to residential
street (Pennsylvania Ave), and not Narbonne Avenue. Ms. Segawa stated that diversion
created traffic congestion problems.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that there was no need for three deputies to attend City
Council meeting, and added that he also seen Deputies cars parked at the City Hall. Mr.
Friedrich stated that he was concerned about the water quality.

Dr. Warren Hemersma, Lomita resident, stated that he has PhD in chemistry and had extensive
experience working at the water quality lab. According to Mr. Hemersma, Cypress Water
Production Facility (CWPF) July report was done under EPA standards, state standards, and
Clean Water Act of 1972. Dr. Hemersma stated that all samples were taken care properly. Dr.

  Page 2
 Hemersma stated that chlorine residuals used at the CWPF at 2 or 2.7 parts per million, which is
consistent with the historical use, iron manganese issue was eliminated completely, Totla
Dissolved Solids are 610 for July, which is within the City goal, while hardness is at the upper
end of what everyone like, but still within the range approved. Mr. Hemersma added that the
issue of methane in the water is not an issues as it is not explosive level.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina thanked Mr. Albert for remodeling the planter area at the Post Office
Memorial site, and thanked Margaret Estrada for her community service over the years.

Councilmember Savidan stated that himself, Councilmember Gazeley and Mayor Estrada
attended on September 5, 2013 dedication of command post at the Sheriff's station.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended Southern California Cities Association of
Governments meeting at which SB 592 was endorsed relating to trade promotion and strategy
to promote California Ports and asked that City Council considers educing SB 592.
Councilmember Gazeley stated that he attended Vector Control meeting, and there was one
more human case of West Nile Virus reported in South Bay sadn aksed people to take
precautions.

Mayor Estrada clarified that when Sheriff’s Deputies park their cars at parking lots in the City
Hall, they stop to write reports/logs.

7. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that he attended the meeting in Santa Monika on September 16,
2013, with State Senator Ted Lieu at which four main issues were discussed including
realignment, Jerry Brown’s proposal to spend from state's reserve to house excess prisoners in
alternate facilities in order to comply with judge’s order, storm water issues and release of bonds
to pay for mandated cost imposed by NS4 regulation, and on-going power outages in South
Bay. According to City Manager Rock, Ted Lou drafted a letter to Southern California Edison
President Theodor Craver in which he referenced his draft legislation from five years ago that
threatened to make utilities liable for monetary damages from power outages if three or more
occurred in the same area within a year.

8. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:

  Page 3
 AYES: Councilmembers Savidan, Traina, Gazeley and Mayor Estrada.
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting held on
  September 3, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  PUBLIC HEARING:

9. INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE –MASSAGE FACILITIES REGULATIONS

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that State legislation passed in 2008 (SB 731) and in
2011 (AB 619) largely eliminated local government’s regulatory authority of massage
establishments in regards to licensing, permitting, and zoning. According to Assistant City
Manager Sugano, since state law went into effect there has been a substantial increase in the
number of massage establishments in the City from 9 in 2008 to 26 in 2013. Assistant City
Manager stated that with the current ordinance in place, owners that were found in violation of
existing regulations reopen massage establishments right away.

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the ordinance was modeled after other local
jurisdictions ordinance in order to strengthen the local oversight. The provisions of the proposed
ordinance include the following: a requirement for a City Registration Certificate for all massage
establishments, businesses shall employ only certified massage practitioners, business owners
and all employees shall possess current registration,  business registration and state
certification shall be displayed at the place of business, permit hours will be reduced from 9 p.m.
to 7 p.m., records of cash register should be kept, exterior windows shall be unobstructed,
license will be revoked if the ordinance is not followed and other restrictions.

Mayor Estrada opened Public Hearing.

David Popelka, Planning Commissioner, stated that implementation of rigorous and strict
regulation would result in more businesses closing their operations in Lomita and therefore, he
apposed introduction of the ordinance.

Mayor Estrada closed Public Hearing.

Councilmember Gazeley stated that the number of massage establishments increased rapidly
over the years and there is illegal activity going on in some of those businesses and City Council
needs to act on that issue.

Assistant City Manager Sugano added that from the zoning point, the City cannot limit the

  Page 4
 number of establishments, but the City could have more control and regulate massage
establishments based on the internal regulatory procedures.

Councilmember Savidan stated that City Council needs to establish stricter regulations and the
rule that the establishments cannot be reopened in the same location for one year if violations
are found seems reasonable.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve item and introduce on first reading an amendment
to the Lomita Municipal Code repealing and replacing Chapter 8 (Massage) of Title VI to
provide for the legitimate regulation of massage businesses and practitioners within the City.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmembers Savidan, Traina, Gazeley and Mayor Estrada.
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

ADJOURNMENT

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
